reviews.scope: meaning of |expression| as nonnegative distance
reviews.reason: Every route, whether distance reading or sign splitting, interprets |ax+b| as a nonnegative magnitude. Without this concept the inequality has no meaning to solve.

reviews.scope: rewrite absolute values piecewise on sign intervals
reviews.reason: The sign-interval route replaces each absolute value by plus or minus the inner expression using this sign rule. A distance interpretation reads solution intervals without the piecewise rewriting.
reviews.counterexample: Solve |x-2|<3 by reading points within distance 3 of 2 on a number line.

reviews.scope: solve affine branch inequalities after fixing signs
reviews.reason: Each sign branch becomes a linear inequality requiring sign-flip care. A distance route can locate endpoints by equations and read intervals geometrically, so the full procedure is route specific.
reviews.counterexample: Rewrite |2x-1|<3 as |x-1/2|<3/2 and read the interval around 1/2.

reviews.scope: tangency of a line to each individual circle
reviews.reason: A common tangent is defined as a line tangent to both circles, so counting them presupposes knowing what tangency to one circle means, namely distance from center equals radius.

reviews.scope: classifying position by center distance and radii
reviews.reason: The tangent counts are indexed exactly by the two-circle position cases, including the coincident equal-radius exception. Classifying position first is intrinsic to the stated criteria.

reviews.scope: deriving tangent existence with perpendicular radii
reviews.reason: Perpendicular radii justify constructing internal and external common tangents. Applying the classification only needs the position cases and tangency notion, so this property serves the derivation route.
reviews.counterexample: Count tangents from recalled position cases, or justify via distance-from-center equals radius.

reviews.scope: domains, punctured domains and function values
reviews.reason: Distinguishing a function value from its limit and preserving punctured domains depends on understanding functions as domain-to-value correspondences. No limit route bypasses this.

reviews.scope: intuitive limiting process via shrinking increments
reviews.reason: Instantaneous rate gives a concrete motivating limit process, but algebraic limit evaluation and continuous extension can be learned without first studying rates of change.
reviews.counterexample: Introduce limits directly through tables of values of (x^2-1)/(x-1) near 1.

reviews.scope: cancelling a removable rational factor before limiting
reviews.reason: Removable rational limits are handled by factoring and cancelling a common factor valid off the limit point. Conjugate, logarithmic and continuity limits do not use this procedure.
reviews.counterexample: Evaluate a log composition limit by continuity without any rational reduction.

reviews.scope: rationalizing radical differences by conjugates
reviews.reason: Conjugate multiplication uses difference-of-squares with radicals, which is this node's skill. Polynomial cancellation and logarithmic limits need no radical manipulation.
reviews.counterexample: A polynomial removable limit is solved by factoring alone.

reviews.scope: combining log differences before infinite-input limits
reviews.reason: The quotient law turns ln(f)-ln(g) into one logarithm whose argument has a limit, enabling continuity. Only logarithmic limit problems use this step.
reviews.counterexample: Rational and radical limits never involve logarithm laws.

reviews.scope: meaning of foci of an ellipse
reviews.reason: Placing the Sun at a focus and distinguishing focus from center presupposes knowing that foci are the two fixed points in the distance-sum definition.

reviews.scope: elliptical orbit application context
reviews.reason: Ellipse applications mention planetary orbits and focal distance, sharing context, but they neither supply the focal placement assumption nor must precede it.
reviews.counterexample: Teach the orbit model directly after the ellipse definition.

reviews.scope: identifying coefficients of corresponding monomials
reviews.reason: Equating coefficients requires recognizing monomial terms and their coefficients, including zero coefficients for absent terms. This is central to the method itself.

reviews.scope: expanding the assumed factor product
reviews.reason: The defining procedure expands the parameterized factor product to obtain coefficients to match. Polynomial multiplication is unavoidable within this named technique.

reviews.scope: prior experience with standard factoring strategies
reviews.reason: Routine factoring builds familiarity with factor forms and checking, but the undetermined-coefficient procedure is a distinct method not requiring mastery of combined standard strategies.
reviews.counterexample: Set (x+a)(x+b) equal to x^2+5x+6 and solve without identity-based factoring.

reviews.scope: cubic unit conversion analogy from metric units
reviews.reason: Metric conversions like 1 cubic decimeter equals 1000 cubic centimeters model the cube-of-factor pattern, but foot-inch cubic units can be understood directly without metric examples.
reviews.counterexample: Derive 1728 by picturing a cubic foot as 12 by 12 by 12 inch cubes.

reviews.scope: computing cube surface area in square inches
reviews.reason: Only the motivating comparison of numerically equal area and volume needs six-face surface area. General foot-inch conversion in any dimension needs no surface area formula.
reviews.counterexample: Convert 3 square feet to 432 square inches without any cube.

reviews.scope: computing cube volume in cubic feet
reviews.reason: The cube volume formula enters only the motivating area versus volume equation. Converting given cubic measurements uses the factor 1728 without computing volumes.
reviews.counterexample: Convert 2 cubic feet to 3456 cubic inches directly.

reviews.scope: evaluating functions and tracking inherited domains
reviews.reason: Composition feeds outputs as inputs, so it requires the input-output correspondence and domain notion; inherited restrictions are unintelligible without the function concept.

reviews.scope: excluding denominator zeros of rational iterates
reviews.reason: Tracking where intermediate denominators vanish is needed when the iterated functions are rational. Compositions of polynomials or other known functions need no fraction-meaning conditions.
reviews.counterexample: Iterate f(x)=2x+1 and reduce indices with no denominators.

reviews.scope: simplifying compound rational compositions
reviews.reason: Simplifying nested rational expressions reveals periodic formulas for rational iterates. Non-rational function iteration does not require rational expression simplification.
reviews.counterexample: Show f(x)=-x has period 2 without fraction algebra.

reviews.scope: probability as a likelihood measure in [0,1]
reviews.reason: Interpreting a measure ratio as a probability and checking its range needs the meaning of probability. The finite counting formula is preparatory analogy, but the meaning itself is necessary.

reviews.scope: solving cut-position inequalities for favorable intervals
reviews.reason: String-cut problems convert length conditions into linear inequalities on the cut point. Area-region problems or directly given favorable segments need no such inequality solving.
reviews.counterexample: Probability a point lands in a drawn sub-square uses only area ratio.
